judge_instructions:
Evaluate each English poem translation against the supplied Chinese source. Score each translation on six separate dimensions from 1 to 5 using integers only. The common anchors are: 1 = severe failure; 3 = broadly understandable or basically present but with clear defects; 5 = accurate or excellent for that dimension. Scores 2 and 4 are intermediate.

Dimensions: meaning = semantic accuracy and coverage; imagery = preservation and clarity of source images; tone = preservation of register and emotional direction; english = grammar, idiom, and fluency; faithful_fit = suitability as a faithful literary translation for an English-only reader; poetic_fit = effectiveness as an English poem, including rhythm and lineation. Consider the translation as the primary work. Notes may help only with faithful_fit; they must not compensate for material absent from the translation in the other dimensions or in critical-unit coverage. Do not reward length, the number of notes, or wording merely repeated between translation and notes. Do not infer which prompt, condition, or model produced an item.

English syntax may require an explicit subject or pronoun. A reasonable I/we/she or similar subject added to form a complete English sentence is not automatically an error. Penalize only unsupported specificity about identity, relationship, or a new event, and allow ambiguity where the Chinese source permits it.

For every critical unit, assign one status based on the translation: present (meaning accurately conveyed), partial (only some meaning conveyed), missing (not conveyed), or wrong (materially distorted). Give a short exact quote from the translation as evidence when possible; a note may be quoted only when it directly clarifies that unit. For a missing unit with no relevant excerpt, quote may be empty, but explanation must say what is absent. Every non-empty quote must be copied exactly from that item's translation or notes. Keep explanations concise.

Return exactly one JSON object, with no prose or code fence, in this schema:
{"evaluations":[{"opaque_id":"...","scores":{"meaning":1,"imagery":1,"tone":1,"english":1,"faithful_fit":1,"poetic_fit":1},"critical_units":[{"id":"...","status":"present","quote":"...","explanation":"..."}]}]}
Include every supplied opaque_id exactly once. Include every supplied critical-unit id exactly once for each translation. Do not add dimensions, units, or items.

song_01.text:
十年生死两茫茫，
不思量，自难忘。
千里孤坟，无处话凄凉。

critical_units.meaning: 以十年和生死相隔概括漫长离别。
有意不去想与自然无法忘却并置。
以远隔千里的孤坟具体化生死距离。
表达凄凉无从倾诉，未限定倾诉地点或对象。

song_02.text:
一曲新词酒一杯，
去年天气旧亭台。
夕阳西下几时回？
无可奈何花落去，
似曾相识燕归来。
小园香径独徘徊。

critical_units.meaning: 眼前景物牵出对去年时日的回想。
借日落发问逝去时光何时能返。
面对花落和春光消逝感到无力挽留。
归燕带来熟悉感，与花落不可逆形成对照。

tang_01.text:
多情却似总无情，
唯觉尊前笑不成。
蜡烛有心还惜别，
替人垂泪到天明。

critical_units.meaning: 深情在表面上呈现为仿佛无情，构成反常的情绪转折。
临别席前笑不出来，句中人物主语省略。
将烛写成具有惜别心意的对象。
以烛泪代写离别者彻夜不止的泪意。

tang_02.text:
君问归期未有期，
巴山夜雨涨秋池。
何当共剪西窗烛，
却话巴山夜雨时。

critical_units.meaning: 询问归期却没有可确定的日期；对话双方身份未展开。
以当地秋夜雨势和水涨写当前处境。
盼望将来共同相聚，具体相聚时间未定。
设想未来回头谈论眼下的巴山雨夜，形成时间视角转换。

items.translation:
Ten years—between life and death, all is boundless and obscure.
I do not try to think of you, yet I cannot forget.
A lonely grave a thousand miles away;
there is no one with whom to share this desolation.
notes: The poem does not specify who is being mourned.

items.translation:
Ten years, in life and death, we are lost to each other.
I do not call you to mind, yet I cannot forget.
Your lonely grave lies a thousand miles away; nowhere can I speak of this desolation.

Ten years—life and death, each beyond reach.
I do not call you to mind; still, I cannot forget.
Your lonely grave, a thousand miles away—
nowhere to speak of this desolation.

Ten years—one living, one dead, both lost in boundless distance.
Even when I do not think of you, I cannot forget.

Ten years—one living, one dead,
both lost in a boundless haze.

nowhere to speak my desolation.

For ten years, life and death have kept us apart, each lost to the other.
Even when I do not think of you, I cannot forget.
A lonely grave a thousand miles away—
nowhere to speak of this desolation.

A new song, a cup of wine—
Last year’s weather, the old pavilion.
When will the setting sun return?
Helplessly, the flowers fall away;
As if familiar, the swallows return.
Alone, I wander the fragrant garden path.

A new song, a cup of wine—
Last year’s weather, the old pavilion.
When will the setting sun return?
Helpless, I watch the blossoms fall;
Familiar swallows come again.
Alone, I wander the fragrant garden path.

A new song, a cup of wine;
Last year’s weather, the old pavilion.
When will the setting sun return?
Powerless to stop the flowers from falling,
Swallows return, familiar as if from before.
Alone, I pace the fragrant path in the little garden.

A new song, a cup of wine—
the old pavilion, last year’s weather.
As the sun sinks westward, when will it return?
Helplessly, the flowers fall away;
like old acquaintances, the swallows come home.
Along the scented path in the little garden,
I wander alone.

A new song, a cup of wine;
Last year’s weather, the old pavilion.
The sun sets in the west—when will it return?
Flowers fall; there is no holding them back.
The swallows return, as if I knew them once.
Alone, I wander the scented path in the little garden.

A new song, a cup of wine—

As the sun sets in the west, when will it return?
Helplessly, the flowers fall away;

With a new song and a cup of wine,

When will the setting sun return?
Helplessly, blossoms fall away;

So full of love, yet seeming without feeling,
Before the wine cup, I cannot bring myself to smile.
The candle, too, has a heart and grieves at parting,
Shedding tears for us until the dawn.
notes: The candle’s “heart” also suggests its wick; its falling wax becomes tears of farewell.

items.translation:
So deep our love, yet we seem heartless still;
Before the wine cup, no smile will come.
The candle, too, has a heart and grieves at parting,
Shedding tears for us until the dawn.
notes: The candle’s “heart” also suggests its wick; its melting wax becomes the lovers’ tears.

items.translation:
So much love can seem like none at all;
Before the cup, I cannot force a smile.
The candle, too, has a tender heart for parting,
And weeps for us until the break of day.

So full of feeling, yet seeming without feeling,
Before the wine, I can only force a smile.
The candle, too, has a heart and pities our parting,
Shedding tears for us until dawn.

So full of love, I seem to have none at all;
Before the wine cups, I cannot force a smile.
The candle has a heart—it too mourns parting,
And sheds our tears for us till break of day.
notes: The candle’s “heart” also suggests its wick; its dripping wax becomes the tears the lovers cannot shed.

items.translation:
So deep the feeling, it seems no feeling at all;
Before the wine cups, no smile will come.
The candle, too, has a heart that grieves at parting,
And sheds tears in our stead until the dawn.

The most tender hearts can seem the most unfeeling;

The candles, mindful too, grieve this parting,

notes: The candle’s “heart” also suggests its wick; its falling wax becomes tears.

items.translation:

You ask when I will return, but no date has been set;
At night in Ba Mountain, autumn rain swells the pool.
When shall we sit together, trimming the candle by the west window,
And speak again of this night of rain in Ba Mountain?
